articles.title: Litter Picking Group Calls Out Supermarkets Over Canal Trolley Issues in Failsworth
articles.excerpt: A litter picking group in Failsworth has urged Aldi, Morrisons, and Tesco to address the ongoing problem of supermarket trolleys being dumped in the Rochdale canal, affecting local waterways and wildlife.
articles.content_html:
A litter picking group in Failsworth has urged Aldi, Morrisons, and Tesco to take action regarding the ongoing issue of supermarket trolleys being discarded in the Rochdale canal. The Clean Up Failsworth Canal group, which has been active for over 13 years, regularly retrieves trolleys and other litter from the waterway as part of their monthly clean-up efforts.

On September 20, the group collected 22 bags of rubbish, 26 nitrous oxide canisters, and 17 supermarket trolleys from the canal. Sandra Ball, a local councillor representing Failsworth West for Reform UK, highlighted the increasing problem of trolleys obstructing navigation for boats, particularly under the bridge leading to the Tesco car park. She stated, "Tesco, Aldi, and Morrisons need to get their act together and get it sorted. We have taken 20 out in one session."

The litter picking group, supported by Oldham Council and the Canal and River Trust, consists of around 90 volunteers. Despite their efforts, members express frustration at the continual littering, with Ball noting that the costs associated with replacing the trolleys ultimately fall on the supermarkets. Lesley Halliday, another volunteer, echoed these sentiments, stating that littering is a persistent issue, particularly from customers of the supermarkets.

In response to the concerns, a Morrisons spokesperson stated that they make efforts to retrieve abandoned trolleys as soon as they are made aware of them. A Tesco spokesperson encouraged customers to return their trolleys after use and mentioned that they employ a specialist company to manage trolley retrieval. The ongoing efforts of the Clean Up Failsworth Canal group aim to improve the local environment and maintain the canal as a pleasant area for the community.
